Schelling’s Tipping Town

Every resident has a mild wish: stay only if at least a third of its neighbours are like it. That is all anyone wants — nobody minds a mixed street. Yet start from a random salt-and-pepper of gold and slate, let the unhappy ones move, and the whole town avalanches into stark blocks — a segregation far harsher than any single mild preference.

rule: random relocation — the headline avalanche (modeled, measured ≈0.75)
⅓ · a third

One mild rule, run to its end. Nobody here is a separatist — each resident is content the moment even a third of its neighbours match, and would happily live in a balanced street. But a balanced street is fragile: a single departure can tip a neighbour below its line, that neighbour moves, and the cascade runs until the map has torn into gold and slate continents. The settled segregation lands near three-quarters — more than twice the wish that caused it. Pull the wish to zero with the knife-switch and the starkness vanishes: no one moves, the colours stay perfectly mixed. The pattern was never in the colours. It was born of the preference. — after Thomas Schelling, 1971.

what is proven · what is modeled self-test …

EXACT — pinned by the live self-test

  • At τ = 0.33 every seeded run settles a segregation index > 0.70 — far above the wish.
  • Neg-control τ = 0 ⇒ zero relocations and index ≈ 0.5 (the random mix, untouched).
  • Under satisfied-swap the like-pair potential Φ is non-decreasing and bounded by E = 4WH−3W−3H+2 ⇒ guaranteed halt.
 

MODELED — watched, not claimed

  • The visible random-relocation hop dynamics — an honest sim of arbitrary moves, not a theorem.
  • That random-rule march to ≈0.75 segregation is measured over seeds; its halt is observed (“when everyone is content”), not the bounded-Φ termination — that proof belongs only to satisfied-swap.
↗ The Drift Jar — its kin: a finite pool that tips to one colour by pure copying-luck, with no wish at all. ↗ The Brazil-Nut Box — “isn’t this the same?” No: that box sorts by size under shaking; this town sorts by a wish.

One mild rule, three exact claims re-run live in the self-test badge above: a τ = 0.33 wish settles segregation past 0.70 every seeded run, a τ = 0 wish moves no one (index stays ½), and the satisfied-swap rule’s like-pair potential Φ only ever climbs toward its ceiling E = 4WH−3W−3H+2 — so it is guaranteed to halt. The headline random-hop avalanche is honest, measured sim, never claimed as a theorem. The page’s core is the byte-twin of core.mjs; the Node test re-extracts it and proves the page === the module.
